summary: Synchronous schema ping from function proxy adds blocking validation hop — p99 end-to-end latency spikes and 10s timeouts for dedicated customer
description:
Issue summary: Customer ScribeAI reports sudden increase in end-to-end request latency (p95/p99) for short chat completions after a recent rollout of a validation change in the function-proxy. Impact: Customer-facing streaming sessions experience long tails and periodic 10s request timeouts. This has escalated to degraded UX for interactive flows.

Observed behavior: During short prompts (<= 64 tokens) we observe p99 latency rising from ~220ms to ~2.1s and occasional 10s timeouts. Traces show an extra synchronous RPC from function-proxy to the schema-validator service during the tool/function call orchestration. The RPC performs a schema/contract validation and an indirect K/V metadata lookup which adds blocking I/O on the request path.

Expected behavior: Schema validation should be async or performed off the hot path (prefetch/validate-on-register) so that per-request latency remains bounded. The function-proxy should not synchronously wait on an external cache miss that triggers DNS and K/V backend calls for every invocation.

Immediate impact: Affected sessions are timing out at the client (10s) and failing fast for interactive users. Customer reports a 12% drop in completed calls and is at risk of pausing dedicated traffic if not remediated.

Temporary workaround: Rolled back function-proxy change on the customer-dedicated cluster to the previous tag which removed the synchronous validation hop. Engineering mitigation applied at 2026-03-13T18:40Z. Longer-term mitigations in progress.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send short streaming chat request to Redwood API with tool invocation metadata enabled
2) Observe trace in X-Ray/Tracing showing synchronous function-proxy -> schema-validator RPC prior to serving-runtime invocation
3) Reproduce p99 spike and intermittent 10s timeout on dedicated customer cluster under light concurrent load (5-20 rps)
4) Toggle schema validation feature flag in function-proxy to confirm regression appearance/disappearance
logs: [2026-03-13T17:12:19Z] api-gateway request_id=abc123 event='client_timeout' code=504 message='upstream request timed out after 10s'
[2026-03-13T17:12:19Z] serving-runtime request_id=abc123 event='request_cancelled' reason='upstream canceled by API gateway'
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: recent merge to function-proxy introduced blocking validation path for tool calls; appears in release notes 2026-03-12 (PR #4892).
Trace analysis: majority of tail latency correlates with schema-validator RPCs that surface a K/V metadata lookup causing an extra 300-800ms per request on hits and 400-1200ms on cache misses.

Network evidence: several RPCs show repeated DNS lookup delays (~200ms) when schema-validator falls back to external metadata service; suggests missing local cache or cold cache behavior in dedicated clusters.
Customer impact: Dedicated cluster had lower warming of validation cache due to isolated traffic patterns; host-level cold-starts exaggerated the effect.
Mitigation applied: Rolled back function-proxy change on ScribeAI's dedicated cluster. After rollback observed p99 fall back to baseline within two minutes.
Next steps: implement async validation path, add local LRU cache in function-proxy, introduce circuit-breaker and metric to detect sync validation hot-paths.

resolution: Partial mitigation: function-proxy rollback applied to customer-dedicated cluster which restored baseline latency. Root cause: synchronous schema validation path that triggers K/V backend and DNS lookups on the hot request path. Follow-up tasks created for non-blocking validation, local caching, and circuit-breaker (linked INT-4220).
